note: Claim: the French reflexive verbs guide covers how pronominal-verb participle agreement runs on the same avoir-style direct-object test, just applied to se instead of le/la/les/que. Target french-reflexive-verbs confirms directly: 'the rule is the same one that governs any participle used with avoir: agreement follows the direct object, and only when that direct object comes before the verb,' and its own FAQ1 repeats 'The OQLF documents this as the same rule that governs any participle used with avoir; the pronominal form doesn't get a separate rule.'
